chunks: He said: Bahr ibn Ziyad narrated from Abdullah al-Kahili that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

If someone comes to you informing you that my son has fallen ill, and he witnessed his death, closed his eyes, washed him, wrapped him in his shrouds, prayed over him, placed him in his grave, and threw dust upon him, do not believe him.
And it is necessary that it be so.
Then Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Tamimi, who was present at the speech in Mecca, said to him: O Abu Yahya, by God, this is a great trial.
Kahili said to him: Then an old man will be concealed from them, and a young man will come to them, in whom is the practice of Yunus.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common kunya for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْكَاهِلِيُّ: Al-Kahili, referring to Abdullah ibn al-Kahili, a companion of the Imams.
key_terms.سُنَّةُ يُونُسَ: The practice or manner of Yunus (Jonah), referring to his concealment or period of absence.
key_terms.فِتْنَةٌ: Trial or test, often referring to a period of confusion or deception regarding religious authority.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the false death report of Imam Musa al-Kadhim in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the critical transition from the era of the Four Deputies to the Major Occultation, where the Shia community faces the 'Great Trial' of verifying the Imam's true status amidst widespread deception. The reference to 'one year of Yunus' alludes to the duration of the Imam's concealment or a specific period of testing, drawing a parallel to Prophet Yunus's time in the whale, symbolizing a period of divine protection and eventual emergence. This event underscores the theological necessity of maintaining faith in the Imam's continued presence despite the absence of clear, public signs.
